items.title: Sheila Jordan — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I was going down working one time with Roswell Rudd, who I used to sing with... I did a, I did a trombone and, and voice thing with him.

ctx.x: Okay. The main reason I do, um… the main reason I let them know this is that… if, if they do a TV show or a radio show somewhere, are you gonna remember who the composers were? And you‟re doing like ten or twelve or fifteen tunes? I don‟t think so. If you have the composer on your sheet music, underneath the title, there‟s no problem. „Cause I know from the shows, the TV shows or the radio, uh, sessions that I do, they bring out a thing, especially in Europe. They want to know who wrote the tune, you know. And…

items.title: Roswell Rudd interviewed by Monk Rowe, Ellenville, New York, June 23, 1998
items.q: His significant recordings include “Flexible Flyer” with Sheila Jordan

ctx.x: Trombonist Roswell Rudd has been instrumental in expanding the language of the jazz trombone. He was born in Sharon, Connecticut on November 17, 1935 and received his first important musician experience in Clinton, New York.

While at Yale, Roswell performed Dixieland music with Eli’s Chosen Six and shortly after started an association with saxophonist Steve Lacy. He has played with and composed new music for a long list of musicians dedicated to expanding the jazz tradition, including Archie Shepp, Charlie Haden and Robin Kenyetta. His significant recordings include “Flexible Flyer” with Sheila Jordan and “Regeneration” with Steve Lacy.
